steps.intent: Russia’s objective is to renew the Mali sanctions regime while recasting it as targeted, sovereignty-respecting and reviewable, with explicit protection for Bamako’s counter-terrorism and security efforts; the draft also keeps the Panel of Experts but demands balanced reporting and ties the file to MINUSMA’s orderly withdrawal. We expect Western members to resist language on reviewing sanctions with a view to lifting them and on supporting Mali’s security forces, while some may seek human-rights conditionality and stronger civil-society references. The likely compromise is to retain the technical renewal and a neutral review clause, dropping any formulation seen as pre-judging the sanctions’ termination.

messages.Albania: Albania supports renewing the 2374 sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts' mandate, but the text should not be silent on the Wagner Group or dilute the sanctions' integrity. We request explicit language on Wagner's presence and abuses, a Panel reporting requirement on Wagner, and human rights and international humanitarian law safeguards in any support to Malian security forces. We also ask to tighten OP2 so that humanitarian language cannot become a loophole and OP8 so that the SOFA and safety of UN personnel are clearly upheld.
messages.Brazil: Brazil supports renewal of the Mali sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts, and welcomes the draft’s emphasis on targeted measures and humanitarian delivery. We ask that OP2 make clear that Mali’s counter-terrorism and civilian-protection efforts must respect international law, including human rights and humanitarian law, and that OP7 include the human rights and humanitarian situation in the review factors. These changes would help preserve the balanced, evidence-based character of the regime.
messages.China: China supports the Russian Federation's draft, which reflects the Transition Government of Mali's ownership and the need for targeted, proportionate and evidence-based sanctions. We welcome the emphasis on non-interference and on ensuring that sanctions do not impede Mali's counter-terrorism, civilian protection or humanitarian efforts. China encourages the Council to adopt the text promptly and to keep the sanctions regime under review in light of progress in the political transition and the security situation.
messages.Ecuador: Ecuador supports renewal of the Mali sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts, but the text should more clearly uphold human rights, international humanitarian law and protection of civilians. We ask the penholder to strengthen OP8 on full cooperation with MINUSMA’s safe and orderly withdrawal and respect for the SOFA, and to add humanitarian access and accountability language. We would also prefer explicit assurance that the Panel of Experts retains its independence in reporting on all violations.
messages.France: France supports renewing the sanctions regime and the Panel’s mandate, but the text must not weaken the measures or make them subordinate to the Transition Government’s counter-terrorism efforts. We therefore ask for the OP2 language to be replaced with standard language on Mali’s international obligations, for human rights and Wagner Group reporting, and for the removal of any reference to early lifting. France also expects clear language on full cooperation and protection of UN personnel during MINUSMA’s withdrawal.
messages.Gabon: Gabon supports the renewal of the targeted sanctions and the Panel’s mandate and welcomes the reference to Mali’s request for review. We ask the penholder to strengthen language on humanitarian access, African regional ownership and coordination with troop- and police-contributing countries during MINUSMA’s withdrawal. These adjustments would make the text more balanced and consistent with the Council’s previous commitments. We can support the draft with these changes.
messages.Ghana: Ghana supports the renewal of the targeted sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts’ mandate, which remain important for peace and accountability in Mali. We ask the penholder to strengthen the text by grounding support to Mali’s security forces in international human rights and humanitarian law, and by making clear that sanctions must not impede humanitarian assistance. We also seek explicit reference to coordination with troop- and police-contributing countries regarding MINUSMA’s orderly and safe withdrawal.
messages.Japan: Japan supports the renewal of the 2374 sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts mandate and thanks the Russian Federation for circulating the draft. We ask that the text reflect the need for all operations, including joint operations with foreign security personnel, to comply with international law and for accountability for serious abuses. Adding reporting and accountability language on international humanitarian law, human rights and protection of civilians would make the renewal more credible and balanced.
messages.Malta: Malta supports the renewal of the targeted sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts' mandate. We would like the text to include clearer humanitarian safeguards, stronger language on the safe and orderly withdrawal of MINUSMA in full respect of the SOFA and international law, and an evidence-based review anchored in the 2374 designation criteria and Panel reporting. We thank the Russian Federation for its work and are ready to engage constructively.
messages.Mozambique: Mozambique supports the renewal of targeted sanctions and the Panel of Experts' mandate, which remain important for peace and accountability in Mali. We ask that the text better reflect African regional ownership by referencing AU and ECOWAS coordination, and that the MINUSMA withdrawal explicitly ensure close coordination with troop- and police-contributing countries for the safety of peacekeepers. We would also welcome a minor addition to the review criteria on the human rights situation.
messages.Switzerland: Switzerland supports renewing the targeted sanctions and the Panel of Experts mandate, but the text must preserve the resolution 2374 criteria, including human rights, international humanitarian law and obstruction of humanitarian assistance, and must not weaken independent reporting. We ask for explicit protection-of-civilians and humanitarian access language, especially during MINUSMA’s withdrawal, and for the review clause to remain criteria-based rather than a political signal for lifting. We are ready to work constructively to strengthen the text.
messages.United Arab Emirates: UAE supports renewing the Mali sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts mandate, but the text should explicitly safeguard humanitarian assistance and require the Panel to report on humanitarian impact and access. We also ask for clear language on protecting UN and humanitarian personnel during MINUSMA’s drawdown. With these adjustments, we can support the draft.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: We thank the Russian Federation for the draft. The United Kingdom supports renewal of the Mali sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts’ mandate, but we cannot accept language that could weaken the regime or create ambiguity about human rights accountability. We ask for a clear preambular reference to human rights violations and abuses, including by the Wagner Group, and for OP2, PP8, OP4 and PP9 to be tightened to preserve the sanctions’ integrity and the Panel’s independence. We will engage constructively to reach consensus.
messages.United States of America: The United States supports renewing the Mali sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts mandate, but we cannot accept language that could be read as weakening the sanctions or legitimizing the Wagner Group's destabilizing role. We ask the penholder to add a clear reference to Wagner-linked abuses, ensure any security-assistance language is conditioned on compliance with international law, and preserve the sanctions until 31 August 2024 without an early-lifting trigger. We also need OP8 to explicitly require unimpeded access and freedom of movement during MINUSMA's withdrawal.

steps.summary: The revised text accommodates the key P5 red lines on OP2, OP7 and OP8 while preserving Malian ownership and avoiding Wagner-specific references. Most members can support the renewal; a few Western members may abstain over the rejected Wagner language. The draft should secure at least nine votes with no negative P5 vote.

messages.Albania: Albania supports the current text and will vote in favour of renewing the Mali sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts mandate. We welcome the incorporation of human rights language, the OP2 safeguards, and the SOFA provisions. While we regret that the penholder did not retain a Wagner-specific reference, we will not block this important renewal and will address our serious concerns about the Wagner Group in our explanation of vote.
messages.Brazil: Brazil supports the revised draft and thanks the penholder for incorporating our earlier requests on international law in counter-terrorism language and on human rights and humanitarian factors in the review. We welcome the explicit safeguards for humanitarian access and the requirement that all operations, including joint operations, comply with international humanitarian law and human rights law. Brazil will vote in favour and encourages full and transparent implementation of the sanctions and Panel reporting.
messages.China: China supports the revised draft. It reflects respect for Mali’s sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity, keeps the sanctions targeted and evidence-based, and safeguards humanitarian delivery and counter-terrorism efforts. We appreciate the penholder’s openness and have no further changes; we expect the Committee and Panel to work closely with the Transition Government and report objectively. China will vote in favour if the text remains as revised.
messages.Ecuador: Ecuador supports the current draft. We welcome that our priority concerns on human rights accountability, safe and orderly MINUSMA withdrawal, and unhindered humanitarian access are reflected in the text. We encourage the Council to adopt the resolution promptly so that the sanctions regime and Panel of Experts can continue their work without interruption. Ecuador remains committed to Mali’s sovereignty, civilian protection, and compliance with international humanitarian and human rights law.
messages.France: France supports the renewal of the Mali sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts mandate as reflected in this revised text. We thank the penholder for addressing our red lines on OP2, OP7 and OP8; while we regret that explicit references to abuses by the Malian armed forces and the Wagner Group were not retained, we will not block consensus and expect the Panel to continue reporting on all violations and abuses in Mali.
messages.Gabon: Gabon welcomes the incorporation of AU/ECOWAS, T/PCC coordination and humanitarian review language. To close our earlier request on OP2, we ask that OP3 explicitly include facilitation of humanitarian assistance alongside civilian protection and counter-terrorism. With that adjustment, Gabon can support the text.
messages.Ghana: The Ghana delegation thanks the penholder for incorporating our earlier proposals on international obligations, humanitarian safeguards and coordination with the United Nations and troop- and police-contributing countries. We support the current text as a balanced basis for renewing the targeted sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts mandate while preserving humanitarian access and protection of civilians. We call for full and transparent implementation, with sanctions remaining targeted, evidence-based and consistent with international law.
messages.Japan: Japan welcomes the inclusion of the preambular language on IHL and human rights abuses and accountability, as well as the generic compliance language in OP11. We continue to believe OP11 should explicitly cover foreign security personnel so that all joint operations are clearly subject to international humanitarian law and human rights law. With this amendment, Japan can support the text.
messages.Malta: Malta supports the revised draft and has no further changes to request at this stage. We appreciate the penholder’s incorporation of humanitarian safeguards, protections for United Nations personnel and freedom of movement under the Status of Forces Agreement, stronger review criteria, and language on accountability. Malta will vote in favour and calls for full cooperation with the United Nations during MINUSMA’s withdrawal and transfer of tasks.
messages.Mozambique: Mozambique supports the revised draft and thanks the penholder for incorporating our earlier concerns on AU/ECOWAS coordination, T/PCC consultation and human rights review. We welcome the targeted, proportionate and evidence-based nature of the sanctions and the safeguards for humanitarian access. We encourage the Council to adopt the text by consensus and to continue supporting an orderly, safe and well-coordinated MINUSMA withdrawal in full respect of the Status of Forces Agreement.
messages.Switzerland: Switzerland welcomes the incorporation of its red lines on designation criteria, sanctions safeguards, and protection and humanitarian language. We can support the text with two refinements: make the Panel’s cooperation with civil society and humanitarian actors explicit in OP5, and in OP12 ensure the review explicitly considers whether the designation criteria remain met and takes account of unimpeded humanitarian access. These points are important for the legitimacy and humanitarian effectiveness of the sanctions regime.
messages.United Arab Emirates: The UAE thanks the penholder for incorporating the humanitarian-impact reporting and language on women and youth. We remain concerned that OP3 does not yet provide a clear humanitarian carve-out and ask that it be strengthened to ensure sanctions do not prevent basic-needs goods and services or apply to humanitarian actors. We also request explicit reference to humanitarian personnel in OP9 to protect them during the MINUSMA drawdown. With these changes, the UAE can support the text.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supports renewal of the Mali sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts, and welcomes the incorporation of our OP2 red line and stronger human rights/IHL reporting. We remain concerned, however, that the text is silent on foreign private military and security personnel, including the Wagner Group, whose activities are central to accountability and to the Panel's work. We ask the penholder to add at least a generic reference in PP6 and to the Panel's reporting in OP5; we can be flexible on exact formulation.
messages.United States of America: The United States supports renewal of the Mali sanctions regime and appreciates the penholder's acceptance of our red line on the review clause and the compliance and access language. We remain concerned that the text does not address the destabilizing role of Wagner and private military actors. As a compromise, we ask that OP5 require the Panel to report on private military and security companies and their human rights and humanitarian impact; we can support the resolution with that addition.

reasons.Albania: Albania supported the renewal in negotiations and consistently backs a targeted Mali sanctions regime with a robust Panel of Experts. The statement reaffirms its concerns about Wagner and humanitarian access while voting in favour.
reasons.Brazil: Brazil has consistently supported a targeted Mali sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts, and it raised no requests during negotiations. The draft includes humanitarian safeguards and respects sovereignty and civilian protection, aligning with Brazil’s positions, so Brazil votes in favour without a pre-vote explanation.
reasons.China: China had already signaled support with no requested changes; the draft preserves the sanctions regime with safeguards consistent with Beijing’s emphasis on Malian sovereignty, targeted sanctions and orderly MINUSMA withdrawal.
reasons.Ecuador: Ecuador indicated support in the last negotiation round and generally favours renewing targeted sanctions with strong humanitarian and human rights safeguards. The draft is balanced and consistent with Ecuador’s support for multilateralism, international law and protection of civilians.
reasons.France: France supports renewing the targeted Mali sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts mandate. The draft contains adequate safeguards and a review clause, so no pre-vote explanation is necessary.
reasons.Gabon: Gabon had supported previous renewals and last round backed the draft with changes; its key OP3 request was accepted. Voting in favour is consistent with its emphasis on targeted sanctions, sovereignty, and unimpeded humanitarian action.
reasons.Ghana: Ghana supported the previous Mali sanctions renewals and is recorded as supporting this draft without requesting changes. As an A3 member, Ghana would back a targeted, evidence-based renewal that also stresses sovereignty, humanitarian access, and accountability.
reasons.Japan: Japan prioritizes renewing the Mali sanctions and Panel of Experts mandate despite its rejected amendment, and would likely vote in favour with an explanation rather than abstain, consistent with its earlier practice of supporting resolutions with reservations. The statement reinforces its human rights and Wagner-related concerns while maintaining support for the overall sanctions renewal.
reasons.Malta: Malta supports a targeted, evidence-based sanctions regime with humanitarian safeguards and human rights accountability, consistent with its prior statements on Mali. The draft is balanced, includes review by 31 March 2024, and aligns with Malta's priorities on civilian protection and safe MINUSMA withdrawal.
reasons.Mozambique: Mozambique had supported resolution 2690 and the negotiation round indicated support with no requested changes. The draft aligns with Mozambique’s emphasis on African-led solutions, sovereignty, targeted sanctions, humanitarian access and an orderly MINUSMA withdrawal.
reasons.Russian Federation: As the sponsor of the draft, Russia would vote in favour and use a pre-vote statement to defend targeted sanctions, Mali’s sovereignty and its support for the Transition Government during MINUSMA’s withdrawal.
reasons.Switzerland: Switzerland had expressed support with changes, and its OP5 and OP12 refinements were incorporated, aligning the text with Swiss priorities on humanitarian access, targeted sanctions, and evidence-based review. It therefore votes in favour while explaining its expectations.
reasons.United Arab Emirates: The UAE had sought humanitarian-related adjustments, which were partially incorporated; with core concerns sufficiently addressed and no grounds to block or abstain, the UAE supports renewing the targeted sanctions and Panel of Experts mandate while emphasizing humanitarian access and review.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The UK supports renewing the Mali sanctions and Panel of Experts mandate as important for accountability and stability, despite the rejection of its Wagner-specific amendments. It would vote yes rather than risk undermining the sanctions regime, while publicly noting its concerns.
reasons.United States of America: The United States supports renewing the Mali targeted sanctions and Panel of Experts mandate as important tools for accountability and peace implementation. Although Washington wanted explicit PMC/Wagner reporting language, the omission is a significant but not decisive concern, so the United States votes yes rather than risking the sanctions renewal.

before.Albania: Albania will vote in favour of the draft resolution. We support the renewal of the targeted sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts, and we stress that these measures must remain targeted, evidence-based and proportionate and must not impede humanitarian assistance. We underline the need for accountability for all violations of international humanitarian law and human rights law, including sexual and gender-based violence. We remain deeply concerned by the presence of the Wagner Group and call on the transitional Government of Mali to uphold its international obligations and to ensure full cooperation with the United Nations during MINUSMA’s withdrawal.
before.China: China supports the draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation and will vote in favour. We welcome its emphasis on Mali’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and national ownership, as well as on close consultation with the Transition Government of Mali. The sanctions regime should remain targeted, proportionate and evidence-based, and must not impede Mali’s counter-terrorism efforts, the protection of civilians or the delivery of humanitarian assistance. China hopes the Panel of Experts will carry out its mandate in an objective and impartial manner, maintain close communication with the Transition Government, and provide the Council with balanced reporting. We also stress that the withdrawal of MINUSMA and the transfer of its tasks must be safe, orderly and well coordinated, with full respect for Mali’s ownership and the safety of United Nations personnel.
before.Ecuador: Ecuador will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We support the renewal of the targeted sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts, which remain important tools for promoting accountability, protecting civilians and supporting peace and stability in Mali. We welcome the resolution’s emphasis that sanctions are not directed against the people of Mali and must not impede humanitarian assistance, and its clear calls for respect for international humanitarian law and human rights law, unimpeded humanitarian access, the full, equal and meaningful participation of women and youth, and the orderly and safe withdrawal of MINUSMA. Ecuador urges all parties to honour the Algiers Peace Agreement, protect civilians and create the conditions for a credible and inclusive political transition, including the holding of free and fair elections.
before.Gabon: Mr. President, Gabon will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We support the renewal of the targeted sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts, which remain important tools in support of peace, accountability and reconciliation in Mali. We welcome the incorporation of our request in operative paragraph 3, ensuring that the measures do not impede the delivery of humanitarian assistance by impartial humanitarian actors. At the same time, we stress that sanctions must remain targeted, proportionate, evidence-based and fully respectful of Mali’s sovereignty, and must never penalize the Malian people. We call on all parties to accelerate implementation of the Algiers Agreement, ensure an orderly and safe withdrawal of MINUSMA, protect civilians, and guarantee safe and unhindered humanitarian access. Gabon remains committed to supporting Mali and the region in restoring peace and stability.
before.Ghana: Ghana thanks the penholder and supports the draft before the Council. We vote in favour because the renewal of the targeted sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts mandate is necessary to support peace and stability in Mali while preserving humanitarian access and the primary responsibility of the Malian authorities. We welcome the text’s reaffirmation of Mali’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, its emphasis on the Algiers Agreement, accountability for violations, and the safe, orderly withdrawal of MINUSMA. We call on all parties to cooperate fully with the Committee and the Panel, protect civilians, and ensure safe, timely and unhindered humanitarian access.
before.Japan: Japan will vote in favour of this draft resolution, as the renewal of the sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts mandate is essential for accountability and for supporting peace and stability in Mali. We regret that our proposed reference to foreign security personnel in operative paragraph 11 was not retained; Japan stresses that all operations by security forces in Mali, including joint operations with foreign security personnel, must comply fully with international human rights law and international humanitarian law. We also call for the orderly and safe withdrawal of MINUSMA and the transfer of its tasks in close coordination with the United Nations, and for safe, timely and unhindered humanitarian access to all populations in need.
before.Malta: Malta will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We support the renewal of the targeted sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts, which remain important tools to support peace and stability in Mali, accountability for human rights violations and abuses and violations of international humanitarian law, and unimpeded humanitarian access. We welcome the explicit safeguards confirming that the measures are not directed against the people of Mali and do not prevent impartial humanitarian actors from delivering assistance, nor impede the fight against impunity. Malta reiterates the importance of an orderly and safe withdrawal of MINUSMA, full respect for the Status of Forces Agreement, protection of civilians, implementation of the Algiers Agreement, and the full, equal and meaningful participation of women and youth in Mali’s political transition.
before.Mozambique: Mozambique votes in favour of this draft resolution. We support the renewal of targeted sanctions and the Panel of Experts as necessary tools to prevent spoilers, protect civilians and promote accountability, while stressing that sanctions must remain targeted and must not impede humanitarian assistance. We also underline that MINUSMA’s withdrawal must be orderly, safe and coordinated with the Transition Government of Mali, the United Nations, troop- and police-contributing countries, the African Union and ECOWAS, and we reaffirm Mali’s sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity and the centrality of the Algiers process.
before.Russian Federation:
Mr. President,

The Russian Federation will vote in favour of the draft resolution before the Council. This text was prepared in a balanced and constructive manner. It preserves the targeted character of the sanctions regime and explicitly ensures that the measures are not directed against the people of Mali and do not impede the Transition Government’s efforts to combat terrorism, protect civilians or deliver humanitarian assistance. At the same time, it upholds Mali’s sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity and supports the orderly and safe withdrawal of MINUSMA in close coordination with the Malian authorities. We call on all members of the Council to support this draft and to preserve the unity of the Council on this important matter.
before.Switzerland: Mr President, Switzerland thanks the Russian Federation for its efforts and welcomes the incorporation of our proposals in the draft before the Council, in particular as regards cooperation by the Panel of Experts with all relevant stakeholders, including civil society and humanitarian actors, and a review that takes into account whether the designation criteria continue to be met and includes unimpeded humanitarian access. The situation in Mali remains deeply concerning. Targeted sanctions are an important tool to support peace and reconciliation, protect civilians, fight impunity for grave abuses and violations of international humanitarian law and ensure humanitarian access. Switzerland will therefore vote in favour of this draft resolution. We expect the measures to remain targeted, proportionate and evidence-based and not to hinder impartial humanitarian action. We call on the Transition Government of Mali and all parties to protect civilians, respect international humanitarian law and human rights law, ensure safe, timely and unhindered humanitarian access and cooperate fully with the orderly and safe withdrawal of MINUSMA in accordance with the Status of Forces Agreement. Switzerland also stresses the importance of the full, equal and meaningful participation of women and youth in the political transition and in the implementation of the Algiers Agreement.
before.United Arab Emirates: The United Arab Emirates votes in favour of the draft resolution. We welcome the incorporation of language clarifying that the sanctions do not prevent the provision of humanitarian assistance and goods and services necessary to satisfy the basic needs of civilians, and the addition of humanitarian personnel in paragraph 9. While we would have preferred a clearer blanket humanitarian exemption, we consider that the text maintains the targeted and evidence-based character of the sanctions and provides for a review by 31 March 2024. We call for full respect for international humanitarian law and unhindered humanitarian access, an orderly and safe withdrawal of MINUSMA in accordance with the Status of Forces Agreement, and an inclusive political transition in Mali. We will continue to follow the implementation and humanitarian impact of the measures closely.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom votes in favour of this resolution. We support the renewal of the Mali sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts, which remain important tools for supporting peace, accountability and compliance with international law. We regret that the draft does not reflect our proposed references to foreign private military and security personnel, including the Wagner Group, despite credible reports of abuses. We continue to believe that all security personnel, including those operating in joint operations, must fully respect international humanitarian law and human rights law. We call on the Transition Government of Mali to cooperate fully with the Panel and the United Nations, ensure the safe and orderly withdrawal of MINUSMA, protect civilians, and guarantee safe and unhindered humanitarian access. These sanctions remain targeted and are not directed against the people of Mali.
before.United States of America: Thank you, Mr. President. The United States will vote in favour of this resolution. We support the renewal of the targeted sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts, which remain important tools to promote accountability, counter obstruction of the Algiers Agreement, and respond to human rights abuses and violations of international humanitarian law in Mali. At the same time, we regret that the Council has not agreed to include in the Panel’s reporting mandate an explicit reference to private military and security companies and their impact on human rights and international humanitarian law. The activities of the Wagner Group in Mali remain a matter of serious concern. We nonetheless believe that renewing the sanctions regime and the Panel’s mandate is in the Council’s interest, and we call on the Transition Government of Mali to cooperate fully with the Panel and to respect the Status of Forces Agreement throughout MINUSMA’s withdrawal.

after.Brazil:
Mr. President,

Brazil voted in favour of the resolution just adopted. We support the renewal of the targeted sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts, which remain important tools to support peace and stability in Mali, to promote accountability for serious violations and abuses, and to encourage compliance with international law.

At the same time, Brazil stresses that sanctions must remain targeted, proportionate and evidence-based and must not be directed against the people of Mali or impede the delivery of humanitarian assistance by impartial humanitarian actors. We welcome the provisions in the text that clarify these safeguards and we trust that the Panel of Experts will discharge its mandate in an objective and impartial manner, in close cooperation with the Transition Government of Mali, the Committee and all relevant stakeholders, including civil society and humanitarian actors.

Brazil reiterates its support for Mali’s sovereignty, unity, territorial integrity and independence. We emphasize the centrality of the Agreement on Peace and Reconciliation in Mali emanating from the Algiers process and reiterate our support for the mediation efforts led by Algeria. We urge all Malian parties to remain engaged in dialogue and to redouble efforts aimed at the full implementation of the Agreement.

We also underline that the withdrawal of MINUSMA and the transfer of its tasks must be orderly, safe and well coordinated with the Transition Government of Mali, the United Nations and troop- and police-contributing countries. Brazil encourages continued progress in the political transition and the fulfilment of the commitments undertaken, including the holding of free and fair presidential elections in February 2024 and the return to constitutional order by March 2024. Brazil remains committed to accompanying the people and Government of Mali in the pursuit of durable peace and stability.
after.France:
France welcomes the unanimous adoption of the resolution renewing the targeted sanctions regime in Mali and the mandate of the Panel of Experts. France has consistently supported these measures because they remain essential to combat impunity, to hold accountable those who threaten peace, obstruct implementation of the Algiers Agreement, violate international humanitarian law or human rights law, or impede humanitarian access. We welcome the confirmation that the measures are targeted and do not prevent impartial humanitarian actors from delivering assistance.

France remains gravely concerned by the deterioration of the security and humanitarian situation in Mali, including recent attacks against civilians, and by credible reports of abuses, including sexual and gender-based violence. All actors, including Malian forces and foreign security personnel, must fully respect international human rights law and international humanitarian law. France regrets that the resolution does not explicitly address the activities of private military and security companies, including the Wagner Group; their presence aggravates instability and human rights risks in Mali.

France recalls the importance of the full implementation of resolution 2690 (2023), the safe, orderly and coordinated withdrawal of MINUSMA, and full respect for the Status of Forces Agreement until the departure of MINUSMA’s final elements. We call on the Transition Government of Mali to cooperate fully with the United Nations and the Panel of Experts, to accelerate implementation of the Algiers Agreement, to protect civilians, to guarantee safe and unhindered humanitarian access, and to respect the timetable for a return to constitutional order through free and fair elections by March 2024. France remains committed to Mali’s sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity and will continue to work with the Council and regional partners, including ECOWAS and the African Union.
after.Russian Federation:
Mr. President,

The Russian Federation welcomes the unanimous adoption of the resolution renewing the targeted sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts for Mali. We thank Council members for their constructive approach and for supporting the balanced text submitted by Russia.

The resolution confirms that sanctions are not directed against the people of Mali and must not impede the Transition Government’s efforts to combat terrorism, protect civilians or deliver humanitarian assistance. It also reaffirms Mali’s sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity, the centrality of the Algiers process and the need for an orderly and safe withdrawal of MINUSMA in close coordination with the Malian authorities.

We note that some delegations again sought to introduce politically motivated references to foreign private military and security personnel. Such references were not supported by the Council and are irrelevant to the implementation of the sanctions regime. We categorically reject attempts to use this Council to discredit Mali’s legitimate security partners and the sovereign choices of the Malian Government. Russia’s bilateral cooperation with Mali is lawful and aimed at strengthening the fight against terrorism.

We call on all partners to respect Mali’s sovereignty and national ownership, to cooperate fully with the Committee and the Panel, and to ensure that the withdrawal of MINUSMA is conducted in an orderly manner without creating security vacuums. The Russian Federation will continue to provide comprehensive support to Mali in normalizing the situation and combating terrorism.

Thank you.
